issues.competing_evidence: Harrison+13 HST-FGS parallax 4.011±0.137 mas and distance 249(+9/−8) pc; Gaia DR2 parallax 3.191±0.069 mas; Schaefer+18 reports 5.4σ disagreement and likely HST systematic error; Gaia EDR3/Bailer-Jones geometric distance 315.407593 [311.865845,318.376343] pc. Sion+15 FUV models use the HST distance.
issues.why_it_matters: Distance changes luminosities and inferred disk Mdot; old FUV solutions cannot be rescaled without a new fit.
issues.needed_action: Retain all measurements separately; decide whether the Sion+15 FUV models should be re-fit at the Gaia posterior distance before using those Mdot values in population summaries.

These cannot safely be averaged or treated as independent epochs.
issues.why_it_matters: Radio variability and population luminosities depend on which reduction/product is used.
issues.needed_action: Check NRAO archive calibrated visibility data or author clarification to map Barrett+20 summary rows to 13B-17A/B and resolve flux-calibration lineage; keep ledger values separate meanwhile.

issues.competing_evidence: Arenas+00 reports q=0.24±0.05, M1=1.2±0.2 M_sun, M2=0.29±0.04 M_sun, i=13±2°; solution assumes Hβ semiamplitude traces the WD, empirical disk line-width/q relations, and a Roche-filling main-sequence donor. Sion+15 also uses M1 grid points; Retter & Naylor compile wider ranges.
issues.why_it_matters: Treating a model-dependent solution as precise component measurements biases CV physical-property distributions.
issues.needed_action: Decide whether these values remain tagged conditional/model-dependent in any community-facing aggregate; do not present them as direct component measurements.

issues.competing_evidence: Barrett+20 gives radio-emission-region B=3210±365 G under a maser interpretation and discusses a possible donor-coronal origin; it separately argues a WD field, if present, must be <1 kG under disk-truncation assumptions. No direct WD surface field found; historical IP/spin claims are unconfirmed.
issues.why_it_matters: Confusing radio-region B with WD surface B would change magnetic-CV classification and population comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep the measurements in separate component/field columns; require direct Zeeman/cyclotron/WD-polar evidence before adopting a WD field.

issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 reports 6.7±1.1×10−13 (1–10 keV) and 4.3±0.4×10−12 erg cm−2 s−1 (0.1–10 keV), derived from catalog information with generic model conversions; asterisk imposes a 10% error floor. Evans+20 is the underlying 2SXPS catalog, not the source-specific fit.
issues.why_it_matters: Cross-population flux/luminosity comparisons can mix absorption conventions, bands and spectral assumptions.
issues.needed_action: Verify the exact source-specific 2SXPS model/NH and Ridder conversion inputs or mark these values as approximate catalog estimates in downstream comparisons.

issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+26 Table 3 and figures list V603 Aql on 2018-01-25; article text associates the epoch with ObsID 19A-166, which appears inconsistent with the calendar date/program context.
issues.why_it_matters: The epoch matters for independent-observation counts and state matching.
issues.needed_action: Resolve the VLA archive program/ObsID and correct the date or identifier if the paper has a transcription error.

issues.competing_evidence: Patterson+97 revisits a historical 23.46(1) or 22.46(1) cycles d−1 claim; its own 1994 data include weak 22.390(5) and 22.82(2) cycles d−1 features, which may be harmonic/sideband or spin-related. issues.why_it_matters: A mistaken spin assignment would affect WD rotation and magnetic-class comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Keep candidates out of the adopted spin field unless later timing/polarimetry uniquely resolves the frequency mode.

references.note: Web/arXiv record inspected. Chandra/RXTE plus archival X-ray study of V603 Aql, published in ApJ 622, 602-612. Finds RXTE data contaminated by Galactic Ridge emission; Chandra HETG spectrum is multi-temperature plasma with high aperiodic variability and weak energy dependence. The paper is used here mainly for X-ray/non-IP context: later radio/FUV papers cite it as evidence against an IP interpretation because V603 Aql lacks the strong energy-dependent X-ray variability typical of IPs. No WD Teff, donor properties, or measured WD magnetic-field strength are taken from it.

Uses Hubble FGS distance 249 +9/-8 pc and E(B-V)=0.10 +/-0.02, models non-truncated optically thick disks because V603 Aql is neither a polar nor an IP, explores Mwd=0.8/1.0/1.2 Msun, and finds Mdot~1.5-2.2e-9 Msun/yr for Mwd=1.2 with roughly factor-two dependence on assumed Mwd.
